taxonomy_note: Workflow routing only. Choose final root-cause taxonomy from supported evidence.

controls.boundary: Entra tenant-independent issuer templates and tenant-stable principal mapping
controls.source_trace: Trace which external tenants may authenticate and which local organization their principals may access. Do not confuse cryptographic validity with tenant admission.
controls.implementation_branch: Bind tid, issuer and client/resource audience using the actual multi-tenant validation rules and tenant enrollment policy. A token signed by a Microsoft key can still originate from an unintended tenant. Supporting multiple tenants is legitimate; show a protected tenant operation accepted for an unassociated identity rather than treating common metadata endpoints as a defect.
controls.operational_method: For tenant-independent metadata, resolve the configured issuer template using the validated tid under the selected token-version/issuer rules; do not accept an arbitrary issuer merely because its signing key is in a shared Microsoft key set. Inspect signing-key issuer restrictions and map identity using the intended tenant-stable identifiers, such as tid plus oid where that is the API contract. Compare identical local-looking subject/object values from two tenants and verify the tenant enrollment decision. General consent grants remain the Entra consent workflow.
controls.controlled_verification: Use two synthetic tenant issuer-template/tid contexts with colliding local-looking principal fields. Compare approved tenant-stable identity mapping with mismatched issuer/key-issuer context before a protected local consumer.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: Multi-tenant login can be intentional; a valid external tenant token is not a bypass without forbidden local access.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Bind issuer/tenant/role admission to local policy and verify authorized onboarding and cross-tenant denial.
